docs.title: Teleoperate a robot arm
docs.text: While you hold HOLD, the arm's end effector follows the motion of your iPhone or iPad: Conduit turns ARKit's pose of the device into geometry_msgs/TwistStamped for MoveIt Servo (/servo_node/delta_twist_cmds by default). A gripper arc works the gripper, and a pose menu sends the arm to a named pose through MoveIt. On a Mac the arm view is view-only.

docs.title: Host setup
docs.text:
Arms need MoveIt Servo from Jazzy or later: the arm profile reads moveit_msgs/ServoStatus and the overlay uses the moveit_servo. parameter namespace, which Humble's Servo publishes and configures differently.

  1. Servo overlay. Load conduit_teleop's Servo overlay after your robot's own Servo parameters, so Servo takes speeds and keeps twists for 0.5 s. The Servo overlay section below shows the file and how to load it.

  2. Time sync. Servo drops a twist whose stamp is older than incoming_command_timeout on its own clock, and it keeps moving on the last twist until then. Conduit therefore stamps every twist, moving or zero, on the robot's clock instead of the device's. It measures that clock from the profile's Joint states topic: the difference between each message's header.stamp and the time it arrives, taking the lowest-latency sample over the last 10 s, and it never stamps a twist ahead of the robot's real time. The 0.5 s stop when the link is lost then holds even when the device's clock differs from the host's, so neither chrony nor Set Automatically is needed for it. The requirements on the Joint states topic:

    • It must be stamped by the computer that runs Servo (the same clock Servo uses), and never in the future. Joint states published by another computer, such as a robot controller while Servo runs on a laptop, are measured as if they were Servo's clock, and Conduit cannot tell.
    • An empty Joint states field is saved as /joint_states. A namespaced topic, for example /arm/joint_states, must be in the field.
    • The host must run on wall-clock time. With simulation time (use_sim_time), HOLD cannot be used.

    HOLD is refused until the robot clock is known. The status line says why:

    Message Meaning "Reading the robot clock from Joint states" Conduit is still collecting stamps (it needs ten Joint states messages). "Robot and device clocks are more than a day apart (simulation time?). HOLD is off." The stamps are not wall-clock time: simulation time, unstamped messages, or a clock that was never set. "Set Joint states in the profile. HOLD needs the robot clock." The profile has no Joint states topic.

    If the robot clock becomes unusable while HOLD is held (a simulator starts, say), the arm lets go and shows "Robot clock changed. Release and press again."

  3. Gripper (optional). A control_msgs/action/GripperCommand server. The profile holds its action name (Gripper action) and, in its Gripper section, the open and closed positions in metres (Open (m), Closed (m); the Franka Panda's fingers travel from 0.0 to 0.04). With Gripper joint set to the finger joint in Joint states, the arm view shows the opening the robot reports.

  4. Named poses (optional). A move_group that publishes the SRDF on /robot_description_semantic and serves /move_action, and Servo's pause service. Conduit sends the moves itself, so there is nothing to install for them, and the profile needs nothing. See Named poses.

When the arm view opens, Conduit calls the profile's Servo command type service (/servo_node/switch_command_type by default) to switch Servo to TWIST, and retries every few seconds while Servo is missing or refuses. The Servo chip shows the result: "Connecting to Servo", "Servo not found", "Servo refused TWIST", then TWIST, or what Servo reports ("Slowing: near singularity", "Halted: joint bound", …), and "Servo not responding" when no Servo status has arrived for a second. HOLD stays off until Servo is ready.

docs.title: The arm view
docs.text:
The arm view runs the Device Pose sensor, which uses ARKit and needs the camera to itself, so opening it pauses the enabled sensors that use the camera (the cameras, except the wide back camera while LiDAR is on, whose images already come from ARKit) and Illuminance. When any of them is enabled, Conduit asks first ("Opening pauses … while the arm view is open. Device Pose uses ARKit, which needs the camera to itself. Continue?"). Closing the view restarts what it paused and stops Device Pose if the view started it.

The wrist camera fills the screen behind the controls. Pinch it to scale between the whole image and filling the screen, and drag to pan where the image is larger than the screen. Each layout keeps its own zoom.

On iPhone the layout follows how you hold the phone; with the rotation lock on, it stays as it is. Turning the phone releases HOLD and stops a gripper drag, and keeps the alignment. Closing the view returns the app to portrait.

  • Landscape, two hands. Along the top: the status chips and the status line, the pose menu and Align, then the gear and close. In the bottom corners, the gripper arc under one thumb and HOLD under the other. Without a Gripper action there is no arc, and HOLD sits in the bottom right corner. An iPad always uses this layout, in any orientation.
  • Upright, one hand. Along the top: the status chips, the gear and close; under them the pose menu and Align. The status line sits above the bottom controls. HOLD is in the bottom corner under the thumb of the hand that holds the phone, with the gripper arc around it.

The status chips: Servo, motion tracking (only while it is not normal, for example "tracking limited (excessive motion)" or "no tracking"), the wrist camera's latency and frame rate ("42 ms · 30 fps") and, when the profile has a Diagnostics topic, the diagnostics. Tap the diagnostics chip to open the diagnostics; this releases HOLD, stops a gripper drag and cancels a pose move. The status line appears only when something needs saying: a fault, a refusal, why HOLD is off, a pose move, or the free-time notice. The camera's captions (STALE, "No data", "No wrist camera topic", …) and the warning that the profile expects other connection settings sit in the space between the controls.

When the top row runs out of room (a smaller iPhone, larger text), the pose menu narrows (a long pose name is cut at its end) down to the width of "Poses", then shows only its symbol, and last Align shows only its symbol.

The gear's panel holds the settings that change the motion:

setting values what it does Max speed 0.5×, 1× (default), 2× Scales translation. At 1× the end effector moves at up to 0.25 m/s. Translation on (default) / off Off sends no translation, so the end effector turns without moving. Rotation on (default) / off Off sends no rotation. Rotation goes up to 1 rad/s. Gripper Left thumb (default) / Right thumb Landscape, with a Gripper action: which bottom corner has the gripper arc; HOLD takes the other. Hand Left hand / Right hand (default) Upright: the hand that holds the phone, which gets HOLD and the arc.

Gripper and Hand are one choice: the hand that holds the phone upright is the one whose thumb has HOLD in landscape. Conduit keeps it per robot on the device. Max speed, Translation and Rotation start at their defaults each time the view opens. The panel is off while HOLD is held.

docs.title: Using it
docs.text:
1. Align. Stand behind the robot's base and face the way its base frame's +x axis points, which is the robot's forward direction. Point the back camera that way, or tilt the device down to watch the screen, down to lying flat with the top of the screen pointing that way, and tap Align: that heading becomes the base frame's +x. If you face the robot instead, the motion is mirrored. Align says why when it refuses: "Tilt the device down: the camera points too far up" (the camera points more than 60° above the horizon), "Point the top of the screen toward the robot's front" or "Wait for motion tracking, then Align". Align again after motion tracking restarts or fails ("Motion tracking restarted. Align again.", "Motion tracking failed. Align again.").
  2. Hold HOLD and move. HOLD is dimmed until the link is up, Servo is ready, the robot clock is known and you have tapped Align. The status line says what it waits for ("Connecting…", a Servo problem, the robot clock, "Starting…"). A press when only Align is missing opens a "Tap Align first" dialog. A press also needs normal motion tracking, and is refused with "Waiting for motion tracking" or "Motion tracking is limited. Move the device slowly." without it. HOLD turns green and reads HOLDING while the arm follows.
  3. Release to stop. Releasing HOLD sends three zero twists at once. Tracking loss, a covered camera, a pose jump or a lost link also stop the arm, with one zero twist ("The pose jumped. Release and press again.", "Motion tracking paused. Release and press again."); release and press again to resume.
  4. Gripper. With HOLD released, tap the arc to open or close the gripper, or drag along it to set an opening. The readout along the arc says "40 % open" ("Moving · 40 % open" while a goal runs). The white handle is the opening asked for, and with a Gripper joint the track fills teal up to the opening the robot reports. Until the opening is known the readout says "Unknown: tap the arc": a drag sends nothing, and a tap opens. The gripper is off while HOLD is held ("Off while HOLD is held"), and a HOLD press while your thumb is on the gripper is refused with "Lift your thumb off the gripper first".

Without Conduit Plus, the status line shows the weekly free time's warnings for a few seconds ("30 minutes of free time left this week", "5 minutes left — the session stops when this week's free time is used up"). When the free time is used up while you hold HOLD or a pose move runs, the arm keeps going until you release HOLD and the move ends, for at most 5 more minutes. Then Conduit stops the arm and shows the Conduit Plus paywall over the arm view; closing the paywall closes the arm view.

VoiceOver: HOLD is the "Clutch" button: double-tap and hold to move the arm, and release to stop. The gripper is the adjustable "Gripper opening": double-tap to open or close it, swipe up or down to open or close it by 10 %, with Open and Close as actions. The wrist camera has "Show whole image" and "Fill screen" actions.

Conduit also publishes the raw pose (<namespace>/pose, /tf) and <namespace>/teleop/clutch (std_msgs/Bool, true while the clutch is held, false on any pose discontinuity), so a custom consumer can move relative to the pose at engage time. The namespace is conduit unless you changed it in Settings. The pose and /tf come from the Device Pose sensor, which runs while the arm view is open.

docs.title: Named poses
docs.text: The pose menu moves the arm to a group state of the robot's SRDF, such as stand or home, through MoveIt. Conduit talks to move_group itself: a pick sends a moveit_msgs/action/MoveGroup goal to /move_action, and Conduit pauses MoveIt Servo for the move. The host needs no extra node and nothing to install for poses, and the robot profile has no pose settings. Named poses work on Jazzy and later.

docs.title: The pose menu
docs.text:
The menu sits next to Align and lists every group state of the robot's arm group, in the order the SRDF has them and with the names exactly as the SRDF writes them (work, stand, ready, home, not "Work"). The pose the arm is at is checked.

  • The button reads the name of the pose the arm is at, or "Poses" when it is at none of them. At a pose it is teal with a checkmark. While the arm moves to a pose, it shows a spinner and the name of the pose you picked. A name longer than the button is cut at its end.
  • Picking a pose moves the arm there at once; there is no confirmation. Picking the pose the arm is already moving to does nothing. Picking another pose while the arm moves cancels that move and starts the new one once the cancel has ended.
  • The menu is off (the button is dimmed and does not open) while HOLD is pressed or held, while the link is down, after the session stopped or the view failed to set up, and for 1 s after the set of poses changes (the SRDF arrived late, or a changed SRDF dropped or reordered a pose). The pause keeps a tap meant for Align from moving the arm. VoiceOver says why: "Off while HOLD is held.", "Off while the robot link is down.", "Off: the session stopped.", "The pose list just changed.".
  • No menu appears without an SRDF that has states for the arm group. The menu appears as soon as the SRDF arrives. The Mac's view-only arm view has no menu.

The arm group is the parent_group of the SRDF's end effector. When several end effectors name a parent group, the first whose group has states counts. Without an end effector, it is the first group that is not an end effector's own group. The gripper's own states (such as open and closed) are therefore not offered. The goals plan for that group. A state name that an SRDF repeats is listed once and moves to the last state of that name, as in MoveIt; two names that differ only in case are two poses.

Conduit reads the SRDF from /robot_description_semantic and sends goals to /move_action, both absolute names. A move_group in a namespace publishes and serves them under that namespace, so the arm view finds no poses and shows no menu.

docs.title: What a pick does
docs.text:
• The goal plans and executes a move of the arm group to the state's joint positions, read from the newest SRDF when the move starts: one joint constraint per joint of the state, at ±0.001 rad, from the arm's current state, with one planning attempt, 5 s planning time, and velocity and acceleration scaled to 0.2.
  • Servo is paused before the goal and resumed when the move ends, whether it succeeds, fails or is cancelled. Conduit uses Servo's std_srvs/srv/SetBool pause service next to the profile's Servo command type service: /servo_node/pause_servo by default. While the move runs, the Servo chip reads "Servo paused for the pose move". Without the pause service, the move still runs. When the arm view connects, Conduit also resumes Servo, in case an earlier session left it paused.
  • The status line reads "Moving to stand…" while the move runs. The checkmark comes from the profile's Joint states topic: the arm is at a pose when every joint of the state is within 0.01 rad (metres for a prismatic joint) of it. Joints compare modulo a full turn, so a joint exactly one turn away from the SRDF value also counts as at the pose.
  • HOLD stops a pose move. Pressing HOLD cancels the move ("Stopping the move to stand…"), and the press does not engage, even if you keep your finger down. Once the move has ended and Servo is resumed, usually well under a second later, the status line reads "Pose move stopped. Press HOLD again.": press HOLD again to move the arm. The arm stops where it is, so the button reads "Poses" until the arm reaches a pose.
  • The background, opening the diagnostics, closing the arm view and the free-time stop cancel the move too, and resume Servo.
  • 30 s after the pick a move that has not ended is cancelled. When move_group does not end a cancel within 5 s, the arm view stops waiting for it.

Cancels need the link

Conduit cancels a move by sending the cancel to move_group, which only works while the link is up. A move running when Wi-Fi drops completes on the host. After the reconnect, the status line reads "Waiting for the move to stand to end…": HOLD stays off and Servo stays paused until the joint states show the arm still for a second (counted from 6 s after the pick, while move_group may still be planning), or 30 s after the pick. Then Conduit resumes Servo.

If the app is killed and opened again while its move still runs, the new arm view knows nothing about that move: it resumes Servo when it connects and allows HOLD while the arm may still be moving. Keep the arm's own emergency stop within reach.

docs.title: Host side
docs.text:
1. Make move_group publish the SRDF. The move_group.launch.py and demo.launch.py that the MoveIt Setup Assistant generates do. A launch file that builds move_group from MoveItConfigsBuilder needs .planning_scene_monitor(publish_robot_description_semantic=True), or the parameter publish_robot_description_semantic: True on the move_group node; it is off by default in Jazzy. Check it with:

    ros2 param get /move_group publish_robot_description_semantic   # Boolean value is: True

  2. Check that move_group serves the MoveGroup action and that Servo has its pause service:

    ros2 action list | grep move_action           # /move_action
ros2 service type /servo_node/pause_servo     # std_srvs/srv/SetBool

docs.title: When a pose move fails
docs.text:
The status line says what happened, until the next pick or HOLD press:

Message What to check "move_group not found on /move_action" move_group is not running, or runs in a namespace. "move_group refused the move to stand" move_group rejected the goal; check the move_group log on the host. "move_group did not answer the move to stand" move_group did not accept the goal, or end a cancel, within 5 s: it hangs or restarted. "The move to stand failed: …" Planning or execution failed; the rest is MoveIt's error code (see below) and, when move_group sends one, its own message after "MoveIt:". Without either, the line reads "The move to stand failed": check the move_group log on the host. "move_group stopped the move to stand" move_group cancelled the goal itself, for example because another client sent it a goal ("…: preempted (-7)"). "The move to stand took over 30 s and was stopped" The 30 s limit. A slow arm needs states closer together. "stand is no longer in the SRDF" A pick waited for a cancel while a new SRDF dropped that state. "stand has no joint values in the SRDF" The state names no joint with one number as its value. "The move to stand was not sent: …" Conduit could not send the goal, for example "Not connected to the robot". "Waiting for the move to stand to end…" The link dropped during the move (see above).

The most useful MoveIt error codes, as the status line shows them after "The move to stand failed:":

Text Code What to do "planning failed (-1)" PLANNING_FAILED No path to the state within 5 s. Move the arm closer with HOLD, or check obstacles in the planning scene. "the pose is in collision or outside the joint limits (-27)" GOAL_STATE_INVALID The group state itself is invalid. Fix it in the SRDF. "the arm starts in collision (-10)" START_STATE_IN_COLLISION The arm is in collision where it is. Jog it clear with HOLD, then pick again. "the controller failed (-4)" CONTROL_FAILED The trajectory controllers on the host refused or aborted the trajectory. Check that they are active (ros2 control list_controllers). "timed out (-6)" TIMED_OUT Execution took longer than the controllers allow. Check the host's controllers. "unknown planning group (-15)" INVALID_GROUP_NAME move_group has no group of the name the SRDF's arm group has: its MoveIt configuration is not the SRDF it publishes.

Other codes read as their short text with the number, or "MoveIt error ".

If the checkmark does not appear after a move, the arm stopped further than 0.01 rad from the state, or the Joint states topic does not carry every joint of the state (ros2 topic echo --once /joint_states --field name).

docs.title: Example: poses that Servo can move from
docs.text:
Servo stops at a singularity ("Halted: singularity" on the Servo chip) and near the joint limits ("Halted: joint bound"). An arm's ready or home state can be singular, and then HOLD does not move the arm after a pick of it. On the six-joint desk arm below (the Maker Arm), both are: the Jacobian condition number at the gripper is 35.2 at ready and 42.2 at home, above Servo's hard_stop_singularity_threshold of 30. Give the arm group states away from singularities and joint limits, and list them first, so they are the first entries of the menu. On that arm, two such states, work and stand, sit before ready and home:

<group_state name="work" group="arm">
    <joint name="link_002_joint" value="0"/>
    <joint name="link_003_joint" value="-0.95"/>
    <joint name="link_004_joint" value="1.2"/>
    <joint name="link_005_joint" value="-0.7"/>
    <joint name="link_006_joint" value="-0.1"/>
    <joint name="link_007_joint" value="0"/>
</group_state>
<group_state name="stand" group="arm">
    <joint name="link_002_joint" value="0"/>
    <joint name="link_003_joint" value="-1.6"/>
    <joint name="link_004_joint" value="1.6"/>
    <joint name="link_005_joint" value="-1.25"/>
    <joint name="link_006_joint" value="0"/>
    <joint name="link_007_joint" value="0"/>
</group_state>

That arm's menu lists work, stand, ready and home, in that order. The condition number is 25.4 at work and 21.7 at stand: between Servo's lower_singularity_threshold (17) and the hard stop, so Servo moves along every axis and slows down near them. To check a state, pick it, wait for the checkmark, hold HOLD and move the device along each axis: the Servo chip should say TWIST or "Slowing: …", not "Halted: …". The values are the desk arm's, measured in simulation; find your arm's with the arm in place, its joints well inside their limits plus Servo's joint_limit_margins.

docs.title: iPad and Mac
docs.text:
An iPad drives the arm like an iPhone, always in the two-handed layout. iPadOS pauses ARKit while Conduit shares the screen with other apps (Split View or a window); the tracking chip then reads "Camera paused: use Conduit full screen", and HOLD stops working until Conduit is full screen again. The diagnostics open in a sheet.

A Mac has no ARKit world tracking, so its arm view is view-only: the wrist camera (pinch and drag work, and it opens on the whole image), the Servo status from the profile's Servo status topic, and the diagnostics, with "Arm control needs an iPhone or iPad. This view shows the wrist camera, Servo and diagnostics." There is no HOLD, gripper, Align or pose menu, and the view pauses no sensors and does not start Device Pose.

docs.title: Servo overlay
docs.text:
conduit_teleop installs a MoveIt Servo parameter overlay at share/conduit_teleop/config/servo_overlay.yaml (source: ros/conduit_teleop/config/servo_overlay.yaml). Build conduit_teleop as described in Teleoperation to get it.

/**:
  ros__parameters:
    moveit_servo:
      incoming_command_timeout: 0.5
      command_in_type: "speed_units"
parameter value what it does moveit_servo.command_in_type speed_units Servo reads the twist as m/s and rad/s, which is what Conduit sends (not unitless −1 … 1 commands). moveit_servo.incoming_command_timeout 0.5 Servo drops a twist whose header.stamp is older than this on the host clock (default 0.1 s). Conduit stamps its twists on the robot's clock and they cross Wi-Fi, so 0.1 s drops many of them; 0.5 s keeps them, and a lost link stops the arm within about half a second (see Time sync above). Releasing the clutch stops the arm at once with explicit zero twists.

The /** key applies the file to any node, so it works whatever your launch file names the Servo node.

Load it after your robot's own Servo parameters. A node applies its parameter sources in order, so the last one wins:

from launch.substitutions import PathJoinSubstitution
from launch_ros.actions import Node
from launch_ros.substitutions import FindPackageShare

servo_node = Node(
    package="moveit_servo", executable="servo_node", name="servo_node",
    parameters=[servo_params, robot_description, robot_description_semantic,
                robot_description_kinematics,
                PathJoinSubstitution([FindPackageShare("conduit_teleop"), "config", "servo_overlay.yaml"])],
)

Check that it took effect (with your Servo node's name):

ros2 param get /servo_node moveit_servo.incoming_command_timeout   # Double value is: 0.5
ros2 param get /servo_node moveit_servo.command_in_type            # String value is: speed_units

docs.title: Drive a mobile robot
docs.text: Conduit sends sensor_msgs/Joy at 50 Hz while the drive view is open and the robot link is up, reliable with KEEP_LAST 1, on the profile's Joy output topic (default /joy). The layout is that of the ROS 2 joy package's game_controller_node, so teleop_twist_joy reads it as it reads a gamepad.

docs.title: iPhone
docs.text:
The drive view follows how you hold the phone: landscape for two hands, upright for one. Turn the phone to switch; with the system's rotation lock on, it stays upright. A turn lets go of every input, so press again to drive.

  • Landscape: status chips at the top left, the gear and close at the top right. At the bottom, the joystick is under one thumb (the left one unless you change it in the gear panel), the mini map is in the other corner, and the status banner is between them.
  • Upright: the same top row, the status banner above the bottom row, the joystick in the bottom corner of the hand that holds the phone (the right hand unless you change it), and the mini map in the other corner.

The chips show the battery, the speed from the odometry, the camera's latency and frame rate (the frame rate only when the robot's and the phone's clocks disagree; "No video" before the first frame; red while the camera is STALE) and the diagnostics (tap it for the full list). The battery, speed and diagnostics chips appear once they have a value. Pinch the camera to scale it between the whole image and filling the screen, and drag to pan it; Conduit keeps the zoom for each orientation. The mini map shows when the profile has a Map or LaserScan topic; tap it for the full-screen map.

docs.title: iPad and Mac
docs.text: The camera fills two thirds of the width, next to a column of Map, Status and Diagnostics tiles. Drag the divider between them to resize (the camera keeps at least 40 % of the width); double-tap it to restore the default. Tap a tile to open it in a sheet. Pinch and drag the camera to zoom it within its tile. With a hardware keyboard connected, the hint "Space + arrows or WASD to drive" shows above the banner. In a narrow iPad window the drive view uses the iPhone's landscape layout.

docs.title: Gear panel
docs.text:
• Max speed: 25%, 50%, 75% or 100% of the stick's full travel, for the forward speed and the turn rate alike. It applies to the on-screen joystick, the keyboard and a game controller's left stick. Every drive view opens at 50%. Changing it while you drive releases every input until you press again, so the robot never jumps to the new speed.
  • Stick (iPhone, landscape): Left thumb or Right thumb for the joystick.
  • Hand (iPhone, upright): Left hand or Right hand, the hand that holds the phone.

Conduit keeps the Stick and Hand choices per robot on this device. The robot keeps driving while the gear panel is open.

docs.title: Map and navigation goals
docs.text:
The full-screen map (a sheet on iPad and Mac) pinch-zooms between 0.5× and 20×, pans with a drag, and resets with a double tap. Nothing drives while the map, Status or Diagnostics is open; the banner says "Paused while a panel is open", and after you close it every input needs a fresh press.

To send a navigation goal, set the profile's Goal pose topic (/goal_pose for Nav2). The profile also needs a Map topic. Then, on the full-screen map:

  1. Tap Set goal.
  2. Touch the goal and drag toward the heading the robot should face. A tap without a drag points the goal away from the robot.

Conduit sends one geometry_msgs/PoseStamped in the profile's Map frame, with a zero stamp (the latest transform), like RViz's 2D Goal Pose tool, and then returns to panning. It waits up to 2 s for a subscriber and then sends anyway. The map says "Goal sent on <topic>", or "Goal sent, but nothing subscribes to <topic>" when no subscriber matched. The goal stays on the map until you close the drive view.

Conduit cannot cancel a goal. Releasing the joystick, closing the map or closing the drive view does not stop the robot driving to it.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
input Joy field role stick up / down axes[1] (up +) linear.x stick left / right axes[0] (left +) angular.z touching the stick, Space, or the left shoulder buttons[9] deadman (enable_button) right shoulder buttons[10] not used: turbo is off, and Conduit masks it unless the deadman is held

See Joy layout for every axis and button.

  • On-screen joystick: the touch input in every case, also with VoiceOver and with a game controller connected. Touch it to drive and lift your finger to stop.
  • Game controllers (MFi and other GameController devices): hold LB / L1 and use the left stick. The "Game controller" chip next to the joystick shows that one is connected; you can use either.
  • Hardware keyboard (Mac, or an iPad with a keyboard): hold Space and use the arrows or WASD. The keys drive at the max speed.
  • VoiceOver: the joystick takes direct touch. It is labelled "Drive joystick" with the hint "Drag to drive; lift your finger to stop", and VoiceOver announces "Driving" and "Stopped".
  • After a lost link, the app going to the background, a closed panel, a turn of the phone or a max speed change, nothing drives until you let go of every input and press again; while you still hold one, the banner says "Release and touch again to drive". While the link is down it says "Disconnected", and while Conduit is inactive "Paused while Conduit is inactive".
  • Without Conduit Plus, a chip over the camera shows the week's free-time notices; tap it to dismiss it. When the free time runs out, the robot stops and the drive view stays behind the Conduit Plus paywall until you close it.
  • The Game Controller sensor publishes <namespace>/joy (/conduit/joy by default); the drive view publishes the profile's Joy output topic (/joy by default). Run conduit_teleop on one of them, not both. If the profile's Joy output is the sensor's topic and the sensor is enabled, Conduit asks before it opens the drive view and pauses the sensor while the drive view is open.

docs.title: Host setup
docs.text:
Install conduit_teleop as described in Teleoperation → Host setup and run it with its default joy_topic (/joy) as described in Teleoperation → Drive view.

conduit_teleop runs teleop_twist_joy with Conduit's parameter file and a watchdog. With the shipped file, full stick is 0.5 m/s and 1.0 rad/s, so the default max speed of 50% tops out at 0.25 m/s and 0.5 rad/s. The watchdog forwards teleop_twist_joy's Twist to cmd_vel while the newest Joy is younger than 0.5 s. When the Joy goes stale it publishes zero twists at 10 Hz for 1 s and then stays silent until Joy resumes (it is also silent before the first Joy), so it does not fight Nav2 or another cmd_vel publisher.

docs.title: Kachaka
docs.text:
The kachaka-api ROS 2 bridge takes velocity on /kachaka/manual_control/cmd_vel once manual control is enabled. On the host, run conduit_teleop's Kachaka launch file, which sets both up and drives at Kachaka's own speeds (Teleoperation → Kachaka). It starts conduit_teleop itself, so use it instead of conduit_teleop.launch.py, not together with it:

ros2 launch conduit_teleop kachaka.launch.py

Profile: Camera /kachaka/front_camera/image_raw/compressed, Map /kachaka/mapping/map, Map frame map, Base frame base_footprint, Goal pose /kachaka/goal_pose, the LaserScan, Odometry and Battery topics the bridge lists, Joy output /joy.

docs.title: Robots
docs.text:
Conduit 3.0 subscribes as well as publishes. A robot profile says which topics hold the robot's camera, map, odometry, battery and diagnostics, and where Conduit sends its commands. Open shows the drive view:

  • Mobile robots — camera, map with the robot's pose and LaserScan, status and diagnostics; drive with the on-screen joystick, a game controller or a hardware keyboard, and set a navigation goal on the map. Conduit sends sensor_msgs/Joy; conduit_teleop turns it into cmd_vel.
  • Robot arms — hold HOLD and move your iPhone or iPad: a MoveIt Servo arm follows, while the screen shows the wrist camera, the gripper, diagnostics and a menu that moves the arm to the poses of its SRDF. On a Mac the arm view only watches.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A ROS 2 host (Humble, Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical or Rolling) reachable over Zenoh or DDS with the same settings Conduit already uses for publishing: Transport, Domain ID and Distribution in Settings. One connection serves the whole app.
  • On the host: conduit_teleop for mobile robots, and Nav2 (or another node that takes a geometry_msgs/PoseStamped goal) for map goals. For arms, MoveIt Servo from Jazzy or later and the Servo overlay, plus a move_group that publishes the SRDF if you want the pose menu.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text:
Tap the robot button in the toolbar, before Recordings and Settings. It is in the same place on iPhone, iPad and Mac. The Robots list opens as a sheet, with the Start button in its bottom corner as on the main screen.

Each robot in the list shows a glyph for its kind, its name, its kind (Mobile robot or Arm), a status line and Open. Tap a robot to edit it; swipe it to delete it.

docs.title: Create a profile
docs.text:
1. Tap +. The editor opens with Kind set to Mobile robot; switch it to Arm for a robot arm. Give the robot a name.

  2. Tap Start in the bottom corner (while Conduit is offline, a "Discover your robot" tip points at it). Conduit goes online and fills in the new profile from the robot:

    • each empty topic field that has exactly one discovered topic of the right type, including Servo's twist topic, command type service and status topic, and the gripper action;
    • the frames: for a mobile robot the Map frame from the map and the Base frame from the odometry; for an arm the Base frame, the Gripper joint and the gripper's Open and Closed positions from the robot's SRDF and URDF.

    Each field is filled once. A field you type in or clear stays as you left it, and a saved profile is never filled again. The list button next to a field shows every discovered topic that fits it. 3. Check the fields. An empty field shows a usual name in grey. Joy output and Goal pose are never discovered, because only the robot subscribes to them: type them if the grey name is wrong. Under Required topics, an empty field is saved as the grey default. Under Optional topics, an empty field turns off what it feeds. 4. Tap Save. An arm's named poses are not part of the profile: the arm view's pose menu lists the group states of the robot's SRDF; see Named poses.

If Conduit finds no topics, the editor shows "No topics found" with the likely causes: the Distribution (Humble vs Jazzy and later), the domain ID, the Zenoh router or the DDS peers, and the profile's connection. You can still type the topic names.

A profile remembers the connection it was made with. If the app uses a different transport or domain, or Humble where the profile was made for a later distribution (or the reverse), the Robots list and the drive view say so ("Profile expects DDS · domain 123 · Jazzy"). The list offers Stop & edit settings, and the editor offers Use the app settings for this profile. Jazzy and the later distributions share one wire format, so switching between them raises no warning. Under each robot the list also shows Offline, how many of the profile's topics are live ("3 of 5 topics live"), or, for an arm, "Servo not found".

docs.title: Open
docs.text:
The Start button is the app's one online switch. Open on an offline app starts it in Publish mode with the sensors you have enabled (none is fine), and so does Start in the Robots list and the editor. If a recording is running offline, Conduit asks "Publish & Record?" first. If the week's free time is used up, the Conduit Plus paywall opens instead of the drive view.

The drive view comes up the way you hold the device and turns with it; the system's rotation lock keeps it as it is. On iPhone, landscape is the two-handed layout and upright the one-handed one, and closing the drive view turns the screen back to portrait. On iPad the arm view always uses the two-handed layout. On iPad and Mac the mobile drive view shows the camera next to Map, Status and Diagnostics tiles (in a narrow window, the iPhone's landscape layout).

Close (×) ends what the drive view started. The app stays online until you tap Stop on the Start button. The drive view also closes when the app goes offline: when the first connection fails, or when the app goes to the background with Background Publishing off.

docs.title: Free time and Conduit Plus
docs.text:
Robots is part of the free plan's 5 hours of use a week. A drive view counts while its robot link is connected; a ROS 2 subscriber to Conduit's topics and a running recording count too. On iPhone and iPad, time counts only while Conduit is in the foreground; a Mac counts in the background too. Each device has its own time, and it refills on Monday at 00:00 local time. The dial around the Start button shows what is left: orange at 30 minutes, red at 5 minutes. Conduit Plus removes the limit.

When the time runs out in a drive view, a held stick, a held HOLD or a running pose move gets up to 5 more minutes to end. Conduit then sends its stop commands, closes a running recording, stops, and shows the paywall over the stopped drive view. Closing the paywall returns you to the Robots list.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
Conduit is not an emergency stop

Releasing the drive controls stops Conduit's commands. That cannot stop a robot whose controller keeps the last command, and it does nothing when the network is gone. Keep the robot's own emergency stop within reach.

  • Mobile robots: letting go of the stick, the game controller or the keys sends Joy with the enable button released. Opening the map, status or diagnostics panel and the app going to the background do the same; after them, and after a lost link, driving needs a fresh press. Run conduit_teleop: its watchdog forwards velocity commands while the newest /joy is younger than 0.5 s. When Joy goes stale, for example because the phone dropped off Wi-Fi, it publishes zero velocity at 10 Hz for 1 s and then stays silent until Joy resumes (it is also silent before the first Joy), so the robot stops without the watchdog fighting Nav2. A map goal is a plain topic message: Conduit cannot cancel it.
  • Arms: releasing HOLD sends zero twists at once. If the link is lost, Servo stops on its command timeout (0.5 s with the overlay). Conduit stamps every twist, the zero ones included, on the robot's clock, which it reads from the profile's Joint states topic, so the stop does not depend on the device's clock being right. HOLD stays off until that clock is known (time sync). A named-pose move is planned and run by move_group on the host. Pressing HOLD, opening the diagnostics, closing the arm view and the app going to the background cancel it, and so does a move that has not ended after 30 s. A cancel needs the link: a move running when Wi-Fi drops completes on the host, and after the reconnect Conduit keeps HOLD off until the arm has stopped, or for at most 30 s from the pick.

docs.title: When something is wrong
docs.text: What you see What to check "No topics found" in the profile editor Distribution (Humble vs Jazzy and later), domain ID, the Zenoh router or DDS unicast peers, the profile's connection "Robot link lost" in the profile editor The link is down ("Router connection lost", "No data from the robot" or "Robot publishers left the graph"); Conduit keeps retrying "Servo not found" in the Robots list Nothing publishes the arm profile's Servo status topic: Servo is not running, or the profile names another node "No data — check Distribution / QoS" The topic exists but nothing arrives: a type mismatch from the wrong Distribution, or QoS "No TF <map frame> → <base frame>" (for example "No TF map → base_footprint") The map → base transform is not published; the map and scan still show. It appears once the map has arrived "Unsupported encoding: X" The camera publishes an encoding Conduit does not draw. It draws JPEG and PNG CompressedImage, and Image in rgb8, bgr8, rgba8, bgra8 and mono8 "Disconnected" in the mobile drive view, "Connecting…" in the arm view's status line The link is down; Conduit reconnects with backoff. Driving needs a fresh touch afterwards, and HOLD a fresh press Red STALE over the camera No camera frame for 0.5 s. The last image stays, dimmed, until frames come back, and the camera chip turns red Camera at 15 fps, or "Paused — device is hot" / "Camera paused: the device is too hot" The device is hot: the camera is drawn at 15 fps when it is seriously hot and stops drawing when it is critically hot. Control is never slowed down "Camera paused: use Conduit full screen" in the iPad arm view iPadOS pauses motion tracking while Conduit shares the screen with other apps. Use Conduit full screen

docs.title: Demo video
docs.text: A demo video of a Kachaka driven from the iPhone and a MoveIt Servo arm following the phone will be added here.

docs.title: Teleoperation with a game controller
docs.text:
Requires Conduit 2.5 or later

The Joy layout and the setup on this page need Conduit 2.5 or later. Settings → About & Help shows your version. Conduit 2.4 and earlier publish an older Joy layout with Best Effort QoS (see the next box).

Conduit's Game Controller sensor publishes sensor_msgs/msg/Joy from any controller paired with your iPhone, iPad or Mac (Xbox, PlayStation, MFi). It publishes on /conduit/joy: the sensor's topic is joy, under Conduit's namespace, which is conduit unless you changed Settings → Namespace (then it is /<namespace>/joy). That is why the commands below pass joy_topic:=/conduit/joy. (Conduit 3.0's drive view uses /joy instead.) On the robot, teleop_twist_joy turns the Joy messages into velocity commands. This page sets that up with conduit_teleop, a ROS 2 package in this repository.

Conduit 2.5 changes the Joy message to the ROS 2 joy layout

From Conduit 2.5, Game Controller publishes Joy exactly like the ROS 2 joy package's game_controller_node. Compared with Conduit 2.4 and earlier:

  • Stick X axes: left is now +1 (it was −1). The Y axes are unchanged (up = +1).
  • Triggers: 0 when released and −1 when fully pressed. They were 0 … +1.
  • D-pad: moved from axes[6] / axes[7] to buttons[11]–buttons[14]. axes now has 6 entries.
  • Buttons: follow the SDL order in the table below. buttons has 21 entries.
  • QoS: Reliable by default, which teleop_twist_joy needs. If you saved Best Effort for the Game Controller in an earlier version, Conduit switches it to Reliable once. You can set it back in the sensor's settings.

If your robot remaps axes or inverts signs to make an earlier Conduit drive correctly, remove that remapping. Otherwise the robot turns the wrong way.

docs.title: Joy layout
docs.text:
The layout is the one that game_controller_node publishes in ROS 2 Jazzy (joy 3.3.0).

index axes[i] value 0 left stick, left / right left = +1, right = −1 1 left stick, up / down up = +1, down = −1 2 right stick, left / right left = +1, right = −1 3 right stick, up / down up = +1, down = −1 4 left trigger released 0, fully pressed −1 5 right trigger released 0, fully pressed −1 index buttons[i] Xbox PlayStation 0 A A Cross 1 B B Circle 2 X X Square 3 Y Y Triangle 4 Back View Share / Create 5 Guide Xbox button PS button 6 Start Menu Options 7 Left stick press LS L3 8 Right stick press RS R3 9 Left shoulder LB L1 10 Right shoulder RB R1 11–14 D-pad up, down, left, right 15–20 always 0

A Siri Remote (Apple TV remote) sends its touch surface as the left stick (axes[0], axes[1]), and its A, X and Menu buttons as buttons[0], buttons[2] and buttons[6].

Conduit publishes Joy at 50 Hz while a controller is connected, and stops when the controller disconnects.

docs.title: Host setup with conduit_teleop
docs.text:
/conduit/joy ──► teleop_twist_joy ──► cmd_vel_in ──► joy_watchdog ──► /cmd_vel
      │                                                   ▲
      └──────────────── Joy freshness ────────────────────┘
  • teleop_twist_joy uses config/teleop_twist_joy.yaml, or the file you pass as params_file. Hold LB / L1 (buttons[9]) to drive. The left stick's up / down sets linear.x and its left / right sets angular.z. Releasing LB sends one zero twist. Turbo is off, because teleop_twist_joy checks the turbo button before the deadman, so a turbo button would drive the robot without LB held.
  • joy_watchdog forwards the twist while the newest Joy is younger than 0.5 s. When Joy stops arriving, it publishes a zero twist at 10 Hz for 1 s and then goes quiet until Joy comes back. That happens when Wi-Fi drops, the controller disconnects, or Conduit goes to the background. teleop_twist_joy alone would leave a robot that keeps its last command moving.

docs.title: Install (ROS 2 Jazzy)
docs.text:
sudo apt install ros-jazzy-teleop-twist-joy
mkdir -p ~/conduit_ws/src
git clone https://github.com/youtalk/conduit-support.git ~/conduit_ws/src/conduit-support
cd ~/conduit_ws
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
colcon build --packages-select conduit_teleop
source install/setup.bash

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
ros2 launch conduit_teleop conduit_teleop.launch.py joy_topic:=/conduit/joy
argument default meaning joy_topic /joy Joy input. The Game Controller sensor publishes /conduit/joy (namespace conduit), so pass joy_topic:=/conduit/joy, or /<namespace>/joy if you changed the namespace. cmd_vel_topic /cmd_vel Where the robot listens for geometry_msgs/Twist. params_file the package's config/teleop_twist_joy.yaml The teleop_twist_joy parameter file. It replaces the shipped file, so start from a copy of it.

At full stick the robot drives at 0.5 m/s and turns at 1.0 rad/s. To change that for your robot, copy the shipped file, change scale_linear.x and scale_angular.yaw in the copy, and pass it as params_file:

cp ~/conduit_ws/src/conduit-support/ros/conduit_teleop/config/teleop_twist_joy.yaml ~/my_robot_teleop.yaml
ros2 launch conduit_teleop conduit_teleop.launch.py joy_topic:=/conduit/joy params_file:=$HOME/my_robot_teleop.yaml

Keep the rest of the copy as it is, including the teleop_twist_joy_node: key. A parameter the file leaves out falls back to teleop_twist_joy's own default, which is not this layout (its default deadman is buttons[5]). To try a speed without restarting, ros2 param set /teleop_twist_joy_node scale_linear.x 0.3 changes the running node.

joy_watchdog parameter default meaning timeout 0.5 Seconds without a Joy before the watchdog takes over. zero_rate_hz 10.0 Rate of the zero twist once Joy is stale. zero_duration 1.0 Seconds of zero twists after Joy goes stale; then the watchdog is silent until Joy comes back.

Sharing cmd_vel_topic with Nav2 or another teleop

joy_watchdog publishes only while you drive and for 1 s after Joy stops, so it does not keep overriding another node once you let go. While you drive, both would publish to the same topic, so for a robot that also runs Nav2 or a second teleop, feed both into twist_mux and use the mux input as cmd_vel_topic.

Not an emergency stop

Neither Conduit nor conduit_teleop is a safety system. Keep the robot's own emergency stop within reach.

docs.title: Drive view
docs.text:
Requires Conduit 3.0

The drive view is part of Robots, which Conduit 3.0 adds. The Game Controller sensor above works from Conduit 2.5.

Conduit 3.0's Robots drive view sends the same Joy layout at 50 Hz while it is open (reliable, KEEP_LAST 1), on the robot profile's Joy output topic, which is /joy by default. For it, launch conduit_teleop with the default joy_topic:

ros2 launch conduit_teleop conduit_teleop.launch.py

The two Joy sources use different topics: the drive view publishes /joy, the Game Controller sensor /conduit/joy. Point conduit_teleop at one of them, not both: the default joy_topic to drive from the drive view, joy_topic:=/conduit/joy to drive with the Game Controller sensor. If you set a profile's Joy output to the sensor's topic, Conduit asks before it opens the drive view and pauses the sensor while the drive view is open.

In the drive view, touching the on-screen joystick (or holding Space on a hardware keyboard, or LB / L1 on a controller) holds buttons[9]. The gear panel's Max speed (25%, 50%, 75% or 100%) scales the stick on the phone, for both the forward and the turn rate. At 100% the parameter file's scales are the top speeds; every drive view opens at 50%, half of them. The watchdog behaves the same for both sources. See Drive a mobile robot for the drive view itself.

docs.title: Kachaka
docs.text:
The kachaka-api ROS 2 bridge takes velocity on /kachaka/manual_control/cmd_vel while manual control is enabled. kachaka.launch.py starts conduit_teleop for it, so run it instead of conduit_teleop.launch.py, not together with it (both would start a teleop_twist_joy_node and a joy_watchdog with the same names):

ros2 launch conduit_teleop kachaka.launch.py
  • cmd_vel_topic is <kachaka_namespace>/manual_control/cmd_vel.
  • params_file is the package's config/kachaka_teleop_twist_joy.yaml, a full copy of teleop_twist_joy.yaml (same axes, deadman and turbo off) with full-stick speeds of 0.3 m/s and 1.57 rad/s. The bridge divides cmd_vel by exactly these maximums, so at Max speed 100% full stick is Kachaka's top speed. At the default 50% the top is 0.15 m/s and 0.79 rad/s. The default file's 0.5 m/s would ask for more than Kachaka's top speed beyond 60 % of the stick.
  • Two seconds after start it calls <kachaka_namespace>/manual_control/set_enabled with true.
argument default meaning joy_topic /joy Joy input: the drive view's Joy topic. kachaka_namespace /kachaka Namespace of the kachaka-api ROS 2 bridge.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The drive view is open but the robot does not move. Check that Joy arrives on the profile's Joy topic: ros2 topic hz /joy. Then check that conduit_teleop listens on that topic (its default joy_topic is /joy) and that you are touching the stick, which is the deadman.
  • Nothing on /cmd_vel while you hold LB, and ros2 topic hz /conduit/joy shows nothing. No Joy reaches the host. Check the topic name (ros2 topic list | grep joy), the domain ID and the transport.
  • The robot turns the wrong way. Remove any axis inversion you set up for Conduit 2.4 or earlier.
  • Nothing on /cmd_vel although Joy arrives. Hold LB (buttons[9]). Check ros2 topic echo /conduit/joy --field buttons while you press it.
  • Over DDS, nothing on /cmd_vel although ros2 topic hz /conduit/joy shows Joy. Over DDS (rmw_cyclonedds_cpp) a Best Effort Joy does not match teleop_twist_joy's Reliable subscription; keep the Game Controller sensor on Reliable. ros2 topic info -v /conduit/joy shows the publisher's reliability. Conduit 2.4 and earlier published Best Effort.

docs.title: Transports: Zenoh vs DDS
docs.text: Conduit 2.0 supports two transports for publishing ROS 2 messages. This page helps you pick one and configure it correctly.

docs.title: Quick Decision
docs.text: Your ROS 2 setup Recommended transport Uses rmw_zenoh_cpp Zenoh Uses rmw_cyclonedds_cpp (default on Humble; opt-in on Jazzy/Kilted/Lyrical/Rolling) DDS Needs to cross subnets / WAN Zenoh (run a router with a public IP) Same-LAN, no bridge infrastructure DDS Corporate network blocking multicast Zenoh (TCP)

docs.title: Side-by-side
docs.text: Zenoh DDS (CycloneDDS) ROS 2 RMW rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_cyclonedds_cpp Bridge required Yes (Zenoh router, rmw_zenohd) No Discovery Via router Multicast, Unicast, or Hybrid Transport TCP (default 7447) UDP (7400 + 250 * domain_id, and neighbors) Cross-subnet Yes No (LAN only) Works through NAT Yes (with router on public IP) No iOS network interface Any reachable interface Must bind to en0 (WiFi) Cellular / VPN Works (TCP egress) Not supported Domain ID range 0-232 0-232 Large messages Router handles fragmentation UDP fragmentation (WiFi may drop) Setup complexity Router needed Direct

docs.title: Configuration at a Glance
docs.text:
Zenoh: - Settings → Transport: Zenoh - Router Address: <host-ip> - Router Port: 7447 - Domain ID: match ROS_DOMAIN_ID on host - Distribution: your host's ROS 2 release (Lyrical by default)

DDS: - Settings → Transport: DDS - Discovery Mode: Hybrid (recommended) / Multicast / Unicast - Unicast Peers: add the ROS 2 host IP (required for Unicast/Hybrid) - Network Interface: en0 (do not use auto) - Domain ID: match ROS_DOMAIN_ID on host - Distribution: your host's ROS 2 release (Lyrical by default)

docs.title: Network Requirements
docs.text:
• Zenoh: iOS device and ROS 2 host must be able to establish a TCP connection to the Zenoh router on port 7447.
  • DDS: iOS device and ROS 2 host must be on the same LAN subnet, with UDP traffic permitted on DDS ports (7400 + 250 * domain_id and adjacent). Multicast reachability is required for Multicast/Hybrid modes. Consumer APs with "AP isolation" enabled will block peer-to-peer UDP — use Unicast mode, or disable AP isolation.

docs.title: When to switch
docs.text:
Use Zenoh if: - You hit fragmentation drops on DDS with large Camera/LiDAR messages. - You need to connect from outside the LAN. - Your WiFi AP blocks multicast and you cannot change it.

Use DDS if: - Your ROS 2 nodes already use CycloneDDS and you don't want to install a Zenoh router. - You want the shortest network path (no extra hop through a router).

See also: - faq.md — setup Q&A - troubleshooting.md — failure modes for both transports - known-issues.md — current limitations

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text:
Common issues and solutions for Conduit.

Which transport are you using? Check Settings → Transport in the Conduit app. Zenoh and DDS have different failure modes. Zenoh issues are under "## Connection Issues" and "## Topic Issues" below; DDS-specific issues are in "## DDS Transport Issues" at the bottom of this page.

docs.title: "Connection Failed: Timeout"
docs.text:
Problem: App cannot reach the Zenoh router.

Solutions:

  1. Verify router is running: 

    # On ROS 2 system
ps aux | grep rmw_zenohd

# If not running, start it
source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash   # or your distro
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd

  2. Check IP address: 

    # Get your ROS 2 system's IP
ip addr show | grep "inet "  # Linux
ifconfig | grep "inet "      # macOS

  3. Update router address in app Settings

  4. Verify same network: iPhone and ROS 2 system must be on same WiFi/LAN

  5. Test connectivity: 

    # From iPhone, ping ROS 2 system
# Or from ROS 2 system, ping iPhone
ping <device-ip>

docs.title: "Connection Refused"
docs.text:
Problem: Router is not listening on port 7447.

Solutions:

  1. Check router is running: See "Timeout" solutions above

  2. Verify port: 

    # Check if port 7447 is listening
netstat -an | grep 7447
lsof -i :7447

  3. Check firewall: 

    # Ubuntu/Linux
sudo ufw status
sudo ufw allow 7447/tcp

# macOS
# System Settings → Network → Firewall → Allow port 7447

  4. Try different port: If 7447 is blocked, configure router with different port

docs.title: "Network Unreachable"
docs.text:
Problem: No network connectivity.

Solutions:

  1. Enable WiFi on iPhone: Settings → WiFi

  2. Connect to same network as ROS 2 system

  3. Check router running: iPhone → Settings → WiFi → (i) → Router address

  4. Restart network:

  5. Toggle WiFi off/on
  6. Restart iPhone
  7. Restart router

docs.title: Topic doesn't appear in ros2 topic list
docs.text:
Problem: Conduit is publishing but topic is invisible.

Solutions:

  1. Verify domain IDs match (most common issue): 
    # Check ROS 2 system domain ID
echo $ROS_DOMAIN_ID

# Check Docker container domain ID
docker exec ros_lyrical_zenoh bash -c "echo \$ROS_DOMAIN_ID"
  2. Domain ID in app Settings must match ROS_DOMAIN_ID on host
  3. Valid range: 0-232 (RTPS specification limit)

  4. Default is 0 if not set

  5. Verify RMW_IMPLEMENTATION: 

    echo $RMW_IMPLEMENTATION
# Must be: rmw_zenoh_cpp

  6. Check the Distribution setting:

  7. Set Settings → Distribution to match your host (Humble vs Jazzy and later)

  8. Restart Zenoh router: 

    # Kill existing router
pkill rmw_zenohd

# Restart with correct domain ID
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0  # Match app's domain ID
ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd

  9. Check app connection state: Should show "Publishing"

docs.title: Topic appears but ros2 topic echo shows no data
docs.text:
Problem: Topic exists but no messages received.

Solutions:

  1. Check for "Waiting for subscriber":
  2. If the sensor row says Waiting for subscriber, Settings → Publishing → Publish only when subscribed is on and no subscription matches the topic. The message count and rate in the next item do not apply to a waiting row.

  3. See Why does a sensor say "Waiting for subscriber"?

  4. Verify sensor is publishing:

  5. Check message count in app (should be increasing)

  6. Rate should be > 0 Hz

  7. Check QoS compatibility:

  8. App uses: Reliability=BestEffort, History=KeepLast(10) by default

  9. Try adjusting in sensor settings

  10. Restart app: Stop and restart publishing

  11. Check the Distribution setting:

  12. Set Settings → Distribution to match your host (Humble vs Jazzy and later)

docs.title: "Camera Permission Denied"
docs.text:
Solutions:

  1. Grant permission:
  2. iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Camera

  3. Find "Conduit" and enable

  4. Restart app after granting permission

docs.title: "LiDAR Not Available"
docs.text:
Reasons:

  1. Device doesn't have LiDAR:
  2. Required: iPhone 12 Pro, iPhone 13 Pro, iPhone 14 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro
  3. iPad Pro 2020 or newer

  4. Apple Vision Pro

  5. Camera permission required: LiDAR uses ARKit which requires camera access

  6. Premium unlock required: LiDAR is a premium feature

docs.title: "Microphone Permission Denied"
docs.text:
Solutions:

  1. Grant permission:
  2. iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone

  3. Find "Conduit" and enable

  4. Restart app after granting permission

docs.title: "GPS Location Services Disabled"
docs.text:
Solutions:

  1. Enable location services:

  2. iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → ON

  3. Grant app permission:

  4. iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → Conduit

  5. Select "While Using the App"

  6. Restart app

docs.title: Sensor shows 0 Hz rate
docs.text:
Problem: Sensor enabled but not publishing data.

Solutions:

  1. Check connection state: Must show "Publishing"

  2. Verify sensor permission: Check iOS Settings → Privacy

  3. Try different sensor: Test if other sensors work

  4. Restart publishing: Stop and start again

  5. Check logs: Look for error messages in app

docs.title: visionOS: No GPS Sensor
docs.text:
Expected behavior: Vision Pro doesn't have GPS hardware (indoor device).

Workaround: Use WiFi positioning if available, or use iPhone/iPad for GPS data.

docs.title: tvOS: Most Sensors Unavailable
docs.text:
Expected behavior: Apple TV only has Game Controller support.

Reason: Apple TV is a stationary device without motion/location sensors.

docs.title: macOS: IMU Not Available
docs.text:
Expected behavior: Macs don't have accelerometer/gyroscope.

Workaround: Use iPhone/iPad for IMU data.

docs.title: Simulator: Mock Data Only
docs.text:
Expected behavior: Simulator generates synthetic sensor data.

Note: Useful for development/testing, but not real sensor readings.

docs.title: ros2 topic echo /conduit/audio fails with "unknown type"
docs.text:
Problem: audio_common_msgs package is not installed on the ROS 2 system.

Solutions:

  1. Use the pre-built Docker image (includes audio_common_msgs): 

    docker run -d -p 7447:7447 --name ros_lyrical_zenoh ghcr.io/youtalk/conduit-support:lyrical
docker exec ros_lyrical_zenoh bash -c \
  "source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash && \
   source /ros2_ws/install/setup.bash && \
   export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp && \
   ros2 topic echo /conduit/audio audio_common_msgs/msg/AudioData"

  2. Install on native ROS 2: 

    sudo apt install ros-lyrical-audio-common  # Lyrical
sudo apt install ros-jazzy-audio-common   # Jazzy
sudo apt install ros-humble-audio-common  # Humble

  3. Build from source if apt package is unavailable: 

    cd ~/ros2_ws/src
git clone --branch ros2 --depth 1 https://github.com/ros-drivers/audio_common.git
cd ~/ros2_ws && colcon build --packages-select audio_common_msgs
source install/setup.bash

docs.title: High battery drain
docs.text:
Causes:

  1. Too many sensors enabled: Disable unused sensors

  2. High publishing rates: Reduce rate for non-critical sensors

  3. Camera/LiDAR active: These consume significant power

Solutions:

  • Enable only sensors you need
  • Reduce rates (e.g., GPS 1Hz instead of 10Hz)
  • Disable camera when not needed

docs.title: App becomes unresponsive
docs.text:
Solutions:

  1. Memory warning: iOS killed background sensors
  2. Check Console logs

  3. Reduce number of active sensors

  4. Network issues: Connection lost

  5. Verify router still running

  6. Check WiFi signal strength

  7. Restart app: Force quit and relaunch

docs.title: Data rate lower than configured
docs.text:
Possible reasons:

  1. Hardware limitation: Some sensors have max rates
  2. IMU: 100 Hz max
  3. Camera: 30 Hz max

  4. GPS: 1-10 Hz typical

  5. Network congestion: Local network can't handle bandwidth

  6. CPU load: iOS throttling due to thermal/battery

Solutions:

  • Reduce rates for non-critical sensors
  • Reduce number of active sensors
  • Check network bandwidth

docs.title: Timestamps seem incorrect
docs.text:
Check:

  1. System time: Ensure iOS device clock is accurate

  2. Timezone: ROS 2 uses UTC, iOS uses local time

  3. Timestamp source: Verify using correct time source (system vs sensor)

docs.title: No topics appear when using DDS
docs.text:
Problem: App shows "Publishing" but ros2 topic list on the ROS 2 host returns nothing.

Solutions:

  1. Restart the cached ros2 daemon first — if you changed RMW_IMPLEMENTATION, ROS_DOMAIN_ID, or CYCLONEDDS_URI in this shell, the daemon is still running with the old context and will lie to you. Run ros2 daemon stop before any of the checks below. See ros2 CLI shows stale topics after changing RMW_IMPLEMENTATION or CYCLONEDDS_URI for the full failure mode.

  2. Verify RMW implementation: 

    echo $RMW_IMPLEMENTATION
# Must be: rmw_cyclonedds_cpp

  3. Check domain IDs match (0-232 valid range for DDS/RTPS): 

    echo $ROS_DOMAIN_ID
    Must match the Domain ID field in Conduit Settings.

  4. Verify network interface binding on iOS:

  5. Conduit Settings → Transport → DDS → Network Interface must be en0 (WiFi).

  6. Leaving this as "auto" frequently fails because iOS may select a cellular or VPN interface.

  7. Multicast blocked by WiFi AP:

  8. Many consumer access points enable "AP isolation" or drop multicast.

  9. Workaround: switch Discovery Mode to Unicast and add the ROS 2 host IP to the Unicast Peers list in Settings.

  10. Firewall on ROS 2 host:

  11. DDS uses UDP ports starting at 7400 + 250 * domain_id (for domain 0: 7400, 7401, 7410, 7411).
  12. Allow UDP on those ports, or disable the firewall for the test LAN.

docs.title: ros2 CLI shows stale topics after changing RMW_IMPLEMENTATION or CYCLONEDDS_URI
docs.text:
Problem: You switched transports (e.g. Zenoh → DDS) or updated CYCLONEDDS_URI (peers, interface, tracing), but ros2 topic list keeps returning the previous transport's results or an empty list.

Cause: The ros2 CLI talks to a long-lived background daemon (_ros2_daemon). The daemon is started with whatever RMW_IMPLEMENTATION / DDS config was in effect at first launch and caches its RMW context — later env-var changes in your shell are ignored until the daemon is restarted.

Fix: Stop the daemon, then let the next CLI invocation start a fresh one in the new environment:

export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=123
export CYCLONEDDS_URI='<CycloneDDS>…</CycloneDDS>'

ros2 daemon stop
ros2 daemon start          # optional — `ros2 topic list` will also autostart it
ros2 topic list

Any time you change RMW_IMPLEMENTATION, ROS_DOMAIN_ID, CYCLONEDDS_URI, or the Peer list, re-run ros2 daemon stop before the next command. This also applies when switching back to rmw_zenoh_cpp.

docs.title: Topics appear but ros2 topic echo shows no data (DDS)
docs.text:
Problem: Discovery works but data does not flow.

Solutions:

  1. QoS mismatch: Conduit uses BestEffort reliability for high-rate sensors (IMU, camera). If your subscriber requests Reliable, it will not match. Use --qos-profile sensor_data or --qos-reliability best_effort on the subscriber: 

    ros2 topic echo /conduit/imu --qos-reliability best_effort

  2. CameraInfo reliability: CameraInfo uses BestEffort with TransientLocal (latchedBestEffort). Standard image_transport subscribers expect Reliable — override the subscriber QoS.

  3. Large messages (Camera, LiDAR): Use Unicast discovery. Multicast reassembly of fragmented RTPS data over consumer WiFi is unreliable — see known-issues.md.

  4. "Waiting for subscriber" on the sensor row: Publish only when subscribed (Settings → Publishing) is on and no subscription matches the topic. Check the subscriber's QoS (best effort, see item 1), or turn the setting off. See On-demand capture.

docs.title: Disconnect takes several seconds (DDS)
docs.text:
Problem: Pressing Stop in the app causes a 2-5 second delay before "Publishing" clears.

Expected behavior: DDS disconnect is serialized to avoid an iOS-specific participant-delete deadlock. See known-issues.md.

docs.title: iOS cannot reach the ROS 2 host (DDS over LAN)
docs.text:
Problem: ping from iOS to host works, but DDS discovery fails.

Solutions: - Confirm both devices are on the same subnet; DDS default transport is UDP, which does not cross routers without configuration. - Corporate networks often block multicast and inter-client UDP. Use a dedicated test LAN or phone hotspot. - On macOS Docker Desktop, the Docker container cannot receive DDS from iOS because Docker Desktop does not provide true host networking. Run the subscriber on Linux, a Parallels VM, or natively on macOS instead.

docs.title: Getting More Help
docs.text:
If your issue isn't listed here:

  1. Check Known Issues
  2. Search existing issues
  3. Ask in Discussions
  4. Create new issue with details
